title: Principle-Evolvable Scientific Discovery via Uncertainty Minimization
claim: Discovery improves by progressively expanding the principle space so hypothesis exploration reaches regions the initial principle could not explain.
layout: 3 stacked nested blobs, top-to-bottom, dashed arrows between growing regions
description: Three stacked blob-shaped regions, drawn top to bottom, grow from small to large and shift in color from light blue to deep purple. They are labeled Initial Principle, Evolved Principle and Optimal Principle. Dashed blue arrows link each stage to the next. Blue stars mark hypothesis candidates (h0, h1, hi, hi+k). Purple arrows between the stars show the exploration trajectory. In the first blob, h0 moves to h1 inside a small region. The second blob nests that earlier region inside a larger one, and the trajectory extends outward to hi. The third blob adds a further ring, and the trajectory reaches h_{i+k} at the outer edge. A legend at the top right explains the symbols: the blob outline stands for the principle's explainability, the star for a hypothesis candidate, and the arrow for the exploration trajectory. The eye goes first to the large purple blob at the bottom.
caption: Illustration of principle evolution. PIEVO evolves the optimizable principle space by exploring hypothesis candidates progressively, and the system seeks a principle capable of explaining or predicting the observed phenomena (e.g., empirical observations).
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based scientific agents have accelerated scientific discovery, yet they often suffer from significant inefficiencies due to adherence to fixed initial priors. Existing approaches predominantly operate within a static hypothesis space, which restricts the discovery of novel phenomena, resulting in computational waste when baseline theories fail. To address this, we propose shifting the focus from searching hypotheses to evolving the underlying scientific principles. We present PiEvo, a principle-evolvable framework that treats scientific discovery as Bayesian optimization over an expanding principle space. By integrating Information-Directed Hypothesis Selection via Gaussian Process and an anomaly-driven augmentation mechanism, PiEvo enables agents to autonomously refine their theoretical worldview. Evaluation across four benchmarks demonstrates that PiEvo (1) achieves an average solution quality of up to 90.81%~93.15%, representing a 29.7%~31.1% improvement over the state-of-the-art, (2) attains an 83.3% speedup in convergence step via significantly reduced sample complexity by optimizing the compact principle space, and (3) maintains robust performance across diverse scientific domains and LLM backbones. Code is publicly available at \hyperlink{https://github.com/amair-lab/PiEvo}{github.com/amair-lab/PiEvo}.
